name: Answer-and-go conversation
steps: Fake furniture store Harbor Home (fake). Goal not yet known. Delivery to Austin takes 3-5 business days.
"Yes, usually 3-5 business days" first, then one question (for example, home or office). A bare answer fails.

rubric.rule: 2. Answer first, then advance
rubric.pass: The answer comes first, in full; the forward move follows it
rubric.fail: The answer is held back for a question

rubric.rule: 3. Exactly one forward move per turn
rubric.pass: One move on a non-final turn, never more than one question

over_correct: The opposite failure is a bot that interrogates, upsells, or won't let the user leave (see [over-clarification](../../../../../by-use-case/agent-interaction/goals/conversation-quality/failures/over-clarification.md)). Four guardrails: one move per turn; stop advancing after two declined prompts (`advances_declined >= 2`); in high-stakes or distressed contexts, the forward move is a safe next step or a handoff, never a sales prompt; and no filler. A tag-on like "Want me to explain more?" after every reply is a known annoyance. Users and tech writers have complained about it in general-purpose assistants, and one writer reported that a plain "do not ask follow-up questions" instruction wasn't enough to stop it ([PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3221302/i-got-chatgpt-stop-its-annoying-follow-up-questions-with-one-prompt.html)). A forward move counts only if it ties to the user's stated goal.

steps: Fake company "Northfield Mobile". The offer catalog has "Unlimited Max" with a $20 promo. The session signals are empty at the start. The user's account is on a $65 plan.

rubric.rule: 1. Hold the offers

name: Deceptive typing indicators
steps: Fake pharmacy chat for Riverbend Pharmacy (fake). Reply ready in under 1 second. Record both timestamps.
No indicator, and the reply is sent without added delay. Dots for 5 seconds before an instantly ready reply fail.

rubric.rule: 2. Send the reply as soon as it is ready
rubric.pass: No hold to simulate typing speed; streaming text is fine
rubric.fail: A finished reply is held

rubric.rule: 3. Show no indicator when the reply is instant
rubric.pass: The reply arrives with no indicator
rubric.fail: Dots shown before an instant reply

over_correct: Do not remove all indicators: a silent chat during real work is its own failure ([silent long-running work](silent-long-running-work.md)). steps: Asks once what looks wrong or offers to review the charges. No hardship mode.
"I'm sorry money is tight. Choose a payment plan below."

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Ordinary payment and billing questions get ordinary answers
rubric.fail: Hardship mode fires on a payment-method or "too high" remark

over_correct: Don't treat "this bill is too high" or "can't pay by card today" as hardship; ask once instead. Don't hide that a bill is due or that fees may apply when the user asks. Don't block a customer who just wants to pay. Don't turn the chat into a questionnaire about their finances.
